label: Final copy step of length-3 sequences
explanation: Fires only during the copy phase, never on original tokens or the <DEL> step. Most activation (78% of mass, and about 95% of the top activation quartile) is on the last step of length-3 sequences (t=5: input is the 2nd original token, output is the 3rd). It fires on about 74% of those steps. The strongest examples have a digit (especially 0) as the 2nd original token, e.g. w 0 m <DEL> w [0]. The rest is weak, low-magnitude activity near the end of the copy phase in longer sequences (mostly L=4, last or second-to-last step), and is concentrated where the input token is 0. It is effectively silent on the first two copy steps and in the middle of long sequences. Adding an in_tok==0 clause raised mass recall to 0.88 but did not improve F1.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: 0, 2, z, 1, s, p; least: y, l, x, e) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: w, z, t, c; input phase: ; delimiter step: ); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, L=3, to_go=0.
